facts.statement: Credit life insurance is insurance on a debtor's life in connection with a specific loan or credit transaction.
facts.quote: means insurance on the life of a debtor pursuant to or in connection with a specific loan or other credit transaction

items.stem: In New Jersey, credit life insurance insures the life of:
options: The lender, against the borrower's default
The collateral that secures the loan
The borrower on a particular loan
The borrower's income while disabled
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:29-2 defines credit life insurance as insurance on the life of a debtor in connection with a specific loan or other credit transaction.

facts.statement: Credit life insurance may be issued only on the term plan, as individual policies to debtors or group policies to creditors.
facts.quote: Individual policies of life insurance issued to debtors on the term plan

items.stem: Under New Jersey law, credit life insurance may be written on which plan?
options: Whole life
Universal life
Endowment
Term
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:29-3 allows credit life insurance only on the term plan, whether as individual policies to debtors or group policies issued to creditors.

facts.statement: Credit life coverage may not exceed the total amount repayable, and on installment debt may not exceed the greater of the scheduled or actual unpaid balance.
facts.quote: The initial amount of credit life insurance shall not exceed the total amount repayable under the contract of indebtedness

items.stem: A borrower signs a car loan with $24,000 repayable in equal monthly installments. He has fallen behind, so his scheduled unpaid balance is $15,000 but his actual unpaid balance is $16,200. Under New Jersey law, the most credit life insurance that may be in force now is:
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:29-4(a)(1) caps credit life on installment debt at the scheduled or actual unpaid indebtedness, whichever is greater. Here that is the actual balance of $16,200.

facts.statement: Credit insurance may not run more than 15 days past the debt's scheduled maturity unless extended at no extra cost to the debtor.
facts.quote: The term of such insurance shall not extend more than 15 days beyond the scheduled maturity date of the indebtedness except when extended without additional cost to the debtor.

items.stem: Unless extended at no added cost to the debtor, New Jersey credit life coverage may last no more than how long past the loan's scheduled maturity date?
options: 15 days
30 days
60 days
6 months
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:29-5 bars the term of credit insurance from extending more than 15 days beyond the scheduled maturity date, except when extended without additional cost to the debtor.

facts.statement: Credit insurance benefits go to the creditor to reduce or pay off the debt; any excess goes to a beneficiary named by the debtor (not the creditor) or the debtor's estate.
facts.quote: any such excess shall be payable to a beneficiary, other than the creditor, named by the debtor or to his estate

items.stem: A debtor dies owing $8,000 on a loan, and the credit life benefit payable is $10,000. Under New Jersey law, how is the benefit paid?
options: $10,000 to the creditor, which refunds the excess to the debtor's estate
$8,000 to the creditor, and $2,000 to the debtor's named beneficiary or estate
$10,000 to the debtor's named beneficiary, who then pays the creditor
$8,000 to the creditor, and $2,000 to the co-signer on the loan
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:29-6(b) requires benefits to be paid to the creditor to reduce or extinguish the unpaid debt, with any excess payable to a beneficiary other than the creditor named by the debtor, or to the debtor's estate.

facts.statement: If credit insurance ends before the debt's scheduled maturity, any refund of what the debtor paid must be paid or credited promptly.
facts.quote: any refund of an amount paid by the debtor for insurance shall be paid or credited promptly to the person entitled thereto

items.stem: A borrower who paid a single premium for credit life pays off the loan two years early. Under New Jersey law, the unearned premium:
options: Must be refunded at the end of the original loan term
Is kept as earned, since the coverage was in force
Must be refunded or credited promptly
Must be credited toward any new loan with the same lender
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:29-8(b)-(d) requires any refund to be paid or credited promptly when the insurance ends before the scheduled maturity date, though no refund below the commissioner's minimum need be made.
items.retired: Answerable by consumer-fairness instinct alone after two rewrites.

facts.statement: The amount charged to a debtor for credit insurance may not exceed the premium the insurer charges.
facts.quote: shall not exceed the premiums charged by the insurer, as computed at the time the charge to the debtor is determined

items.stem: An insurer's premium for a borrower's credit life coverage is $300, and the lender adds $50 on top as a service charge for the coverage. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Allowed, since lenders may mark up credit insurance
Allowed, if the markup is disclosed in writing
Not allowed, unless the loan is over $25,000
Not allowed, since the debtor's charge may not exceed the insurer's premium
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:29-8(b)-(d) bars charging a debtor more for credit life or credit health insurance than the premiums charged by the insurer.

facts.statement: The creditor may not be designated as the insurer's claim representative for adjusting credit insurance claims.
facts.quote: The creditor shall not be designated as claim representative for the insurer in adjusting claims

items.stem: Under New Jersey's credit insurance law, who may NOT be designated to adjust claims for the insurer?
options: The creditor
The insurer's own claims staff
An independent adjuster the insurer designates
A third-party administrator the insurer designates
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:29-10(c) bars designating the creditor as claim representative for the insurer in adjusting claims.
items.retired: Odd-one-out cue (creditor vs three insurer-side options) with no balanced rewrite.

facts.statement: When credit insurance is required as security for a debt, the debtor may furnish it through existing policies or through any insurer authorized in New Jersey.
facts.quote: have the option of furnishing the required amount of insurance through existing policies of insurance owned or controlled by him

items.stem: A lender requires life insurance as security for a loan. The borrower already owns a large term policy with another authorized insurer. Under New Jersey law, the borrower:
options: May use the existing policy, on request to the lender
Has to buy coverage from an insurer the lender selects
May use the existing policy if the lender's insurer first declines him
May use the existing policy if it is issued by the lender's insurer
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:29-11 gives the debtor the option of furnishing required insurance through existing policies he owns or controls, or through any insurer authorized in New Jersey.
items.retired: Answerable by consumer-fairness instinct alone after two rewrites.
